chapter: Rhythm Club memories and playing technique
title: Rhythm Club jam sessions in all keys; Cuban Bennett

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Jerry Preston's. It was an after-hour place. After hour spot there on 132nd between 7th and Lenox. Jerry Preston's After Hour Spot. Then of course there at the Rhythm Club, those jam sessions was just something. They could start off with nothing, maybe piano, drums and trumpet. Before the night's over, or the day, whatever they get together, it would be 10, 11 pieces there jamming. And not only on one tune. They would play one tune and then segue into another tune, and go from one key right on through the whole thing chromatically, every key, go through all keys.
That's interesting, because what sessions there are now....
They generally pick out their pet keys?
Well their pet keys and the tune might go for an hour.

Well the tunes that they were playing went that long. Every other chorus it would be another key and there used to be a trumpet player, used to hang everybody around him, and that was Benny Carter's cousin, boy named Cuba.
Yeah, Cuban Bennett, that's right, and played changes, every four bars, every two bars, and run everybody crazy. Cuban Bennett, that's right.
Did you get to play with him much?
No, I never did play with him, but I heard him a couple of times.
Yeah, he's one of these legendary people.
Yeah, Benny mentioned him when he did his oral history interview. Benny I guess was a great one for picking odd keys.

Oh yeah, all keys. Don't get up there and start jamming with those guys if all you can play is in C or B flat, E flat. They're gone, they're gone in E, A, B natural, anything, just go on and start playing. See, sometimes they pick those tunes with a lot of changes. See and then get in those difficult keys. See you're playing B natural and start scuffing around, or E natural or A, you know.

That's right. F sharp was a piano player's key too. Yeah, don't fool around up there. Like with Stuff Smith, we used to be there, of course we were playing at the Onyx Club and guys used to come in and want to sit in and Stuff would tell them right quick, 'no, don't jump
up on this bandstand if you can't play." You know, cause we're liable to play anything. Don't jump up here if you can't play and swing, don't come up here. He'd bring everybody down.
